title: Status OK / Standby
fullDescription: A single flash on the diagnostic LED indicates the control board is powered and idle with no faults.
safetyWarning: Turn off power at the breaker before opening the unit. HVAC systems contain high-voltage components and refrigerant under pressure.

causes.cause: Loose wiring or connector at terminal block
Sensor or thermistor out of calibration

symptoms: 1 flash displayed on diagnostic LED or controller
Unit will not start or shuts down quickly
Indoor or outdoor fan behavior abnormal

fixSteps.title: Power Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the breaker for 5 minutes, then restore power and observe whether the code returns.

fixSteps.title: Visual Inspection
fixSteps.instruction: With power off, open the service panel and inspect connectors, sensor leads, and contactors for damage or looseness.

fixSteps.title: Call Technician
fixSteps.instruction: If the fault persists after a reset and visual check, contact a licensed HVAC technician for component-level diagnosis.

repairTime: 30 minutes to 3 hours depending on root cause
whenToCallPro: Call a licensed HVAC technician if a power reset and basic inspection do not clear the fault, or any time refrigerant or sealed-system work is required.

faq.a: Only the power reset and visual checks are DIY-safe; component diagnosis or refrigerant work requires a licensed technician.
Typical service calls run $150-$500; sealed-system or compressor work can exceed $1,500.
If the unit is not heating or cooling at all, treat it as urgent. If it self-recovers, schedule service soon to prevent recurrence.

title: Low Pressure Switch Open
fullDescription: Eleven flashes on a Goodman defrost board indicate the low-pressure cutout opened. Common in cooling with dirty filter; in heating with iced coil or charge loss.

fixSteps.title: Thaw
fixSteps.instruction: Run emergency heat 30 min if iced.

faq.a: Yes, switch is auto. Board may lock out after 3 strikes.

title: High Pressure Switch Open
fullDescription: Twelve flashes report the HPS opened. Outdoor fan failure, dirty coil, or overcharge typical causes.
whenToCallPro: Check capacitor too — common Goodman fan-stop cause.

faq.a: Yes — Goodman fan caps fail often. Check before replacing fan motor.

safetyWarning: Discharge line is hot (200F+) - do not touch.

title: Outdoor Coil Sensor Failure
fullDescription: Thirteen flashes flag the outdoor coil temp sensor outside valid range. Goodman boards revert to time-based defrost.

fixSteps.title: Locate
fixSteps.instruction: Bottom return bend of outdoor coil.

whenToCallPro: Wire damage may need pigtail repair.

faq.a: Yes, on time-based defrost - less efficient.

title: Reversing Valve Solenoid Open
shortDescription: Reversing valve solenoid coil open or unplugged.
fullDescription: Fourteen flashes indicate Goodman board energized reversing valve but no current flow detected.
symptoms: Heat pump cools when set to heat (or vice versa)
whenToCallPro: If valve body stuck, brazing required.

faq.a: Yes - cheapest fix on a reversing valve.

title: Defrost Cycle Active
fullDescription: Fifteen flashes are a status code, not a fault. Indicates the unit is currently in a defrost cycle (3-10 min). Reversing valve is in cooling, outdoor fan is off, indoor aux heat is on.

faq.a: Yes - frost on outdoor coil melting.

title: Compressor Lockout - Hard
fullDescription: Sixteen flashes mean Goodman board locked out the compressor due to 3 strikes of the same fault (HPS or LPS). Manual reset required.

fixSteps.title: Identify root
fixSteps.instruction: Check what fault came before lockout.

whenToCallPro: Repeated lockouts = leak or component failure.

title: Brownout Lockout
fullDescription: Seventeen flashes indicate Goodman defrost board sensed line voltage too low. Compressor disabled until voltage recovers.
whenToCallPro: Utility issue if voltage low at meter.

faq.a: Yes, when voltage stable above 200V for 5 min.

title: Compressor Run Capacitor Weak
fullDescription: Eighteen flashes appear on newer Goodman/Amana ComfortNet units that monitor run cap microfarads. Cap aged below threshold means imminent failure.
whenToCallPro: Always discharge before touching cap terminals.

faq.a: $15-40 part. One of the cheapest HVAC repairs.

safetyWarning: Discharge capacitor with 20k ohm resistor before handling.

title: Auxiliary Heat Active
shortDescription: Status: indoor electric/gas backup heat is energized.
fullDescription: Nineteen flashes are informational on Goodman heat pumps with W2 backup heat. Triggers during defrost or below balance point.
symptoms: Higher electric bill in cold weather

faq.a: If running above 40F, check thermostat balance point setting.

title: Defrost Lockout - 4 Hour
shortDescription: Defrost terminated by max-time 3x in 1 hour.
fullDescription: Twenty flashes are a defrost-specific lockout. Defrost ran to max time without coil clearing 3 times in 1 hour - usually low charge or stuck reversing valve.

faq.a: Yes, after 4 hours - but failure will repeat without fix.
